summary: Console shows negative usage balance for API key after retention compact and large tracehook header split
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported that one of their API keys shows a negative usage credit balance after a retention compaction ran overnight. The negative balance is visible in the Console usage ledger and reflected in the daily billing snapshot. The customer is concerned this will affect monthly invoices and quota enforcement.

Impact:
- One API key for Clippe r Analytics shows -12,340 token credits for 2026-03-11 to 2026-03-12 in Console and the usage CSV export.
- Affected key belongs to a Dedicated tenant. No model inference failures reported, only analytics/billing artifacts.
- Customer-facing dashboards show sudden credits refund and subsequent quota recalculation for routes tied to the key.

Environment:
- Prod (dedicated) region: us-east
- Customer tenant ID: CA-2241 (provided by customer)
- Console version: 3.7.2
- Ingest pipeline version: ingest-processor@v2026-02-28

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer and reproduced by Support):
1) Exported Console usage CSV for API key CA-2241:apiKey-5pkg for 2026-03-10..2026-03-12.
2) Noted negative row for 2026-03-11 (-12,340 tokens) with route_label "/realtime/streaming".
3) Queried raw events via internal usage-query service for the same timeframe and saw two sets of sessionize entries for many streaming requests (same requestid but split across two records).
4) Verified retention compaction job ran 2026-03-12 02:10 UTC which rewrote hourly rollups for 2026-03-11.

Observed behavior:
- During compaction, some streaming events with very large tracehook headers (>32KB) were split at the tracehook proxy and produced two ingest messages. The compaction rollup then merged the partial records incorrectly, subtracting duplicated refunds when deduplicating by session id, leading to negative aggregated token counts for the day.
- Console UI shows -12,340 and the exported CSV matches the UI. Billing pipeline picked up the compacted ledger and applied a credit adjustment in the accounting snapshot service (staged, not yet invoiced).

Expected behavior:
- Retention compaction should not introduce negative net usage. Large tracehook headers should be preserved or normalized to avoid splitting sessionization keys. Deduplication should prefer last-write semantics that avoid double-counting refunds.

Relevant logs/attachments:
- Support attached truncated usage CSV and sample raw event IDs: ev-9f3b, ev-9f3c, ev-9f3d.
- Ingest-processor logs around 2026-03-12 02:07-02:12 UTC show "tracehook: header chunked" warnings for many messages.
- Compaction job trace: compact-job-20260312-02:10 (job logs attached to internal runbook).

Investigation notes:
- Engineering repro: We reproduced splitting by sending deliberately large tracehook headers via a streaming client; ingest-proxy currently chunks at 32KB and emits chunked records with identical requestid but missing sequence metadata for re-assembly.
- Dedup logic in hourly rollup assumes either identical token counts or a canonical sequence token; chunked partials caused one partial to have negative delta when merged due to how session delta is computed.
- Early hypothesis: two interacting bugs: (1) tracehook proxy chunking without reassembly metadata, (2) rollup dedup/merge using additive inverse when encountering partial session resets.

Workaround (customer-visible):
- Disable very large custom tracehook headers on the client (short-term mitigation). Customer has turned off a verbose X-Trace-Context blob in their streaming clients and reports no new negative rows in a short test.
- Internal workaround: we can re-run a targeted compaction/repair for the affected hourly range to recompute the rollups from raw events if we first reassemble chunked records using requestid and timestamp heuristics. This is a manual/ops action and requires coordination with Billing/Accounting teams.

Next steps / action items:
- [ENG-1] Add reassembly metadata (chunk sequence id and total_length) to tracehook proxy emitted messages (owner: ingest-proxy team).
- [ENG-2] Patch compaction rollup to treat partial-session merges as "incomplete" and prefer raw-event recompute rather than in-place inverse subtraction (owner: ingest-processor).
- [OPS-1] Schedule a one-time repair compaction for tenant CA-2241 for 2026-03-11 hourly bundles after safeguards are validated (owner: Support ops + Billing).
- [CS-1] Keep customer informed; provide an ETA and confirm manual repair before invoice finalization.

Resolution notes (pending):
- Engineering has a small PR to add chunk metadata: github.com/redwood-inference/tracehook-proxy/pull/122 (in review).
- A patch to compaction dedup logic is in draft: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-processor/pull/425.
- Support scheduled a repair run tentatively for 2026-03-15 pending signoff from Billing.
